draft.title: Leonardo da Vinci
card: Leonardo da Vinci (1452 to 1519) was an Italian painter, inventor and scientist. He worked in Florence and Milan, and later in France.
He filled thousands of pages of notebooks with drawings and notes. They show studies of the human body, plants, water and flight, and designs for machines.
Many of his machines were only designs on paper. His notebooks show how closely he observed the world and tried to understand it.
Leonardo is often seen as a model of the Renaissance ideal of a person skilled in many fields, who builds knowledge and talent in art and science.
draft.remember: Leonardo's notebooks show one mind working in art, science and invention.

a.q: Why is Leonardo da Vinci often used to show the Renaissance ideal of a person skilled in many fields?
opts: He worked in art, science and invention
He painted more pictures than any other artist
He was paid by the Medici family of Florence
He invented the printing press used in Europe
a.why: Leonardo's notebooks and paintings show skill in art, science and invention. Painting alone does not fit the ideal, because the ideal is about skill across many fields, not the number of works in one field.
a.clue: Think about what his notebooks and paintings cover together.

b.q: Ava is studying a page from Leonardo's notebooks. It shows a careful drawing of a human arm with notes on the muscles. What does this page best show about Leonardo?
opts: He studied the body as a scientist as well as an artist
He only drew pictures to please rich patrons
He built working machines from every design he drew
He had no interest in science or in how things work
b.why: The detailed drawing and notes on muscles show he observed and studied the body, which is scientific work as well as art. The page does not show he built every design, because many of his machines stayed on paper.
b.clue: Look at what the notes and the drawing study together.

a.best: He worked in art, science and invention

b.best: He studied the body as a scientist as well as an artist

problems.detail: All three wrong options use absolute words ('no interest', 'only', 'every'), while the right option is the only measured one. A student could pick it by ruling out the absolutes without knowing the idea.

a.q: Why is Leonardo da Vinci often used to show the Renaissance ideal of a person skilled in many fields?
opts: He worked in art, science and invention
He painted more pictures than any other artist
He kept his work to painting and drawing
He spent his whole working life in Florence
a.why: Leonardo's notebooks and paintings show skill in art, science and invention. Painting a large number of pictures does not fit the ideal, because the ideal is about skill across many fields, not the number of works in one field.
a.clue: Think about what his notebooks and paintings cover together.

b.q: Ava is studying a page from Leonardo's notebooks. It shows a careful drawing of a human arm with notes on the muscles. What does this page best show about Leonardo?
opts: He studied the body as a scientist as well as an artist
He drew the arm as an artist, not to study how it works
He studied the muscles as a scientist, not as an artist
He drew the arm as a design for a new machine
b.why: The careful drawing is the work of an artist, and the notes on the muscles show he was studying how the body works, which is science. Choosing artist or scientist alone misses half of what the page shows, and the page studies a real arm rather than a machine design.
b.clue: Look at what the drawing and the notes each tell you.
